records.title: UK Right of Abode
records.text: I started the process of obtaining my Right of Abode in the UK back in 2019.  It started off with a web search, where I found ICS and then a phone call with them about my options.  Things started moving forward and then Covid hit; I put the process on the back burner.I started trying to communicate with ICS again in late 2021, but we were unable to connect.  There wasn't much communication from them.  This was in the late winter of 2021.Ultimately, in early 2022, I started a chat with a team member on their website.  They were very apologetic and after that the lines of communication were good again.  ICS provided guidance on the necessary documents that are required, which I obtained.  They then helped me start the application on the UKVI site, as well as preparing a legal letter from them to support my application.  The process was moving expeditiously.  I made the necessary appointments and was awarded my Certificate for the Right of Abode in June, which is fixed inside one of the pages of my USA passport.Overall, ICS was very helpful and communicative, except for the aforementioned period of time.  They are generally easy to reach via chat, email, or phone and generally reply within 24 hours (although, there were a few times I had to write multiple emails to get a response).I would recommend using ICS for Visa & Immigration services, and will use them again for guidance when I need to obtain a renewal for my Right of Abode.

records.title: INFORMATION PROVIDED ON ICS REQUEST HAS NOT BEEN SUBMITTED TO IMMIGRATION
records.text: Dear all,In a nutshell the services offered by ICS is a con. The outer package looks sophisticated especially when you receive a request form asking for 21 pieces of  evidence supporting your application (EU settlement scheme). Just after submission of the application my passport data was lost and I was kindly asked to resubmitted to ICS . Several weeks after receiving acknowledgment  of application submission, Immigration office was asking us for a basic documents which had already been submitted to ICS. Question raised by Immigration brought to our attention that the application may not have been submitted properly. ICS was not been able to provide us  evidence of complex application submitted in our behalf. The information provided were standard exactly the same as in online form. What was the most upsetting ? The time we spent on gathering 21 pieces of evidence. It took us more than 1.5months to put all those documents together. Some of the documents  required costly certified translation some of them required IT support to dig them out from multiple digital sources. It was so frustrating that all our effort went down the drain..ICS have not even acknowledge the issue nor apologies for the situation.

description:
Courmacs Legal Ltd is a law firm based in Blackburn, UK, specialising in civil litigation and consumer claims. Our experienced team is dedicated to helping clients navigate complex legal matters with a focus on Personal Contract Purchase (PCP) claims, business energy claims, housing disrepair claims, and undisclosed commission claims.

As a no-win, no-fee firm, we strive to ensure that clients face no financial risk when pursuing claims. We work diligently to provide transparent, efficient, and professional legal services, keeping clients informed every step of the way. Our goal is to resolve claims as swiftly and smoothly as possible while maintaining the highest standards of care and communication.

At Courmacs Legal Ltd, we are dedicated to helping clients achieve positive outcomes while treating every case with the care and attention it deserves.

records.title: fraudulent use of old data to form an “agreement”
records.text: With the recent claim with PCP ongoing I have raised a complaint directly to my finance provider. In October last year I received an email from this company stating they have been instructed to represent me. When I questioned this they simply sent me a document stating the fees I’d have to pay should I break the agreement which I did not make. They said there was a 14 day cooling of period which I missed, shock they emailed me just after this!? The document had all incorrect information on there and even had an address I have not lived in since I was a young child, this address was listed as one of my most recent addresses! If this was raised by my why would I include an address that had no finance at, I don’t even think I had a bank account at that age. When I asked for more information about how they obtained this they simply told me upon investigation they have withdrew my case with no cost applied.it took me to threaten to speak to the legal ombudsman and the ICO about my data being obtained to get this to happen. I am still none the wiser as to how they obtained my information and I have had no further contact from my finance provider so I am concerned this has ruined the claim I submitted directly a year ago! How many other people are they doing this to who get fooled into going with it out of fear of getting a fine. I am just utterly shocked by the fact they have details I can’t even remember. I hope this has been completely withdrawn now and has not messed with the complaint my have been dealing with directly!

Our team of experienced lawyers has established strong connections with internationally recognised solicitors and barristers, providing our clients with access to a global network of legal resources.

With our deep knowledge of the law and our extensive network of legal professionals, we are able to offer our clients a comprehensive range of legal services that are tailored to their individual needs.
⭐️ 550+ 5 star reviews from our clients on google

I would definitely recommend them to anyone who needs any advice or help! Thank you so much for all your help APL. :)

records.title: Excellent service
records.text: Adam dealt with a dispute matter for me. The advice provided was clear, honest and thorough. I cannot praise Adam highly enough as he is an efficient and reliable person to have represent you. Thank you for your help and I highly recommend Adam for all personal and business needs.

records.title: Innovative.
records.text: 5*. The innovation says it all.

records.title: The Amazing lawyers at the Adam Prudens…
records.text: The Amazing lawyers at the Adam Prudens Law provided me the best legal advise I could have asked for. The professionalism and dedication make them best solicitors around. This is brilliant law firm truly a gem!

records.title: Adam Prudens Law
records.text: Adam Prudens Law: A Complete FraudThis so-called “law firm” is nothing but a scam. They claim to have international offices, but it’s all a lie—they’re just renting virtual spaces that aren’t even manned. They present themselves as a “top-tier firm,” but here’s the truth: they’re NOT regulated solicitors.I lost £1,800 to this sham, but I’m not letting it slide. I’ve already reported them to:Action FraudHMRCTrading StandardsCompanies HouseASASRAAdam Prudens Law looks legitimate with a polished website and convincing sales pitch, but it’s all smoke and mirrors. Adam, you might be good at conning people, but you’ll need that silver tongue when you’re explaining yourself in a prison cell. Don’t forget to say hi to P. Diddy while you’re in there.This guy is 24 years old, hasn’t even been in business for a year, and likely doesn’t have any real legal qualifications. Everything about this “firm” is fake—fake offices, fake reviews, fake credentials. Don’t fall for it. Sending them your ID or money is a mistake you’ll regret.Adam, with your sales skills, you could’ve done something worthwhile, but instead, you chose to scam people. Now, you’ll face the consequences.For anyone considering using Adam Prudens Law—don’t. This isn’t just a bad service; it’s a criminal operation. Protect yourself and your money, and steer clear. Adam, enjoy the karma that’s heading your way.

records.title: RUDE
records.text: Very rude man at this company, he can’t own the company as the way he speaks to people is disgusting and disrespectful.  If it is his company he won’t be in business for much longer …..

records.title: Very bad customer service
records.text: Very bad customer service, very rude.  Messaged me on WhatApp, firstly calling me the wrong name, no apology, then didn’t even know what he messaged me for.  Told me to go use another firm.  So I did.  His loss

description: For two decades, DC Law has been providing a client-focused, nationwide service across its three UK offices. Courtesy of expert teams of solicitors, licensed conveyancers and legal executives, our clients are able to enjoy a supportive service focused on making every step of their home move matter as refreshingly straightforward as it can be.

records.title: Thank you to Iain Flemming
records.text: Thank you to Iain Flemming who has been super supportive throughout our journey to completing the purchase of our new home. You are a fountain full of knowledge and we hope you prosper and grow in your career even further. Many thanks again.

records.title: Thanks DC Law
records.text: Thanks DC Law, you are the best. Most especially Chris Stone is very helpful all the way, so much appreciate your team work.

records.title: Exceeded Expectations
records.text: We used DC Law and had Harry Cotton as our conveyancer. Harry far exceeded my expectations that I had based on my first purchase, where my previous conveyancers were infrequently updating me, slow to respond etc. Harry and DC Law have been completely different. Harry was on the ball, if I rang the phone he’d pick up. If I had a question, he’d have the answer. He made sure to frequently give me and my partner updates. Very helpful and couldn’t recommend enough.

records.title: Excellent service
records.text: We would not hesitate to recommend dc law to anyone, but we need to give a special mention to our conveyancer Amy Amory who has supported and helped us throughout our home buying process. Amy has been conscientious, efficient, hardworking and never too busy to reply to a phone call or e mail. Her patient and calm manner have made a very stressful process very manageable and dc law should be very proud to have such an outstanding employee. Thank-you so much Amy and best wishes for the future

records.title: Hayley Geall was exceptional
records.text: Hayley Geall was exceptional! She was efficient, professional, available with excellent attention to detail. We moved in less than 7 weeks and just in time for Christmas in our new home! Highly recommend Hayley for conveyancing. Thank you so much Hayley!

records.title: Great service
records.text: Jennifer Oakes dealt with my case and the service was of the highest standard. She was always at the end of the phone to answer any questions and explain any queries. All actions were completed immediately and I would use this company again without hesitation. Thank you Jenny.

records.title: Great service
records.text: There was a couple of complications regarding the sale of our property and dc law went that extra mile. Must say a big thank you to Rebecca Stonehouse who really was brilliant and kept us informed all the way. Every issue was dealt with promptly and she dealt with us with consideration and respect.Mr & Mrs Beck

records.title: DC Law has been nothing but…
records.text: DC Law has been nothing but professional as they have dealt with the sale of my deceased mother's property. A special thanks must go to Megan Koxha who worked tirelessly to ensure the sale went as smoothly as possible and was particularly supportive when a nasty problem arose in the final weeks. Her professionality and calm helped to make the situation easier and she ensured the sale was completed correctly. Thank you!

records.title: Probate sale - professional and empathetic
records.text: I would highly recommend Lisa Rimmer from DC Law. Lisa expertly helped with the probate sale of my late mum’s house with professionalism, empathy and compassion. Lisa kept me fully informed of what was happening and when and also what next to expect. I found the whole process emotionally draining (due to it’s nature) but Lisa helped keep the wheels in motion expertly!

records.title: Great experience for probate sale
records.text: We dealt with DC Law for the probate sale  of my mother’s property. Our case handler Lisa Rimmer worked sensitively and expertly. Despite the first sale falling through it was reassuring to keep the same contacts. Lisa kept me well informed and updated, and was attentive to queries. Thank you for making this difficult process much easier.

records.title: My experience with DC law and in…
records.text: My experience with DC law and in particular, Rachel Samosa has been very good. She was professional at all times but was also friendly and approachable in her manner. I felt confident with her handling our case.

records.title: Superb support on sale of property
records.text: Working with Cheryl England on the sale of my late brother’s home was long and arduous due to probate issues and that I live in California. Cheryl was diligent, informative and provided timely explanations on the processes required for the sale of the property and I was confident with the work she performed.

records.title: Good service but need the right person.
records.text: The service provided by Shirena was excellent. she was very efficient and pro-active. Communication was first rate.

records.title: Thank you Esther!!
records.text: Esther in the main was polite and helpful.Really pushed so that we exchanged as needed. Everything went extremely smoothly on completion, with Esther checking in on us all the way.Would recommend.

records.title: Good. Conveyancing experience
records.text: Our case handler was Rachel Samosa who guided us through the sale of my late fathers property. Rachel was always responsive to our queries in a polite professional way.

records.title: Slow start, good finish
records.text: Once reviews of progress became frequent on my part, my house sale progressed well. I did have a very slow start, but the solicitor became easy to contact via phone or email once I pointed out difficulties. The online portal is very clear to understand and follow for progress.

records.title: A very smooth selling process
records.text: A very smooth selling process.  A simple to use online portal and a dedicated person on the phone.

records.title: Helpful and patient
records.text: This was a long and difficult sale mainly due to fire regs work needed on the block of flats which took some time to resolve. Rebecca Rees was helpful, patient and constructive throughout the process. It was usually easy to get in contact with her and in the end completion went through very smoothly.

records.title: Good comms
records.text: Nancy picked up our case and dealt with in an efficient, helpful and professional basis.  She communicated with us on a regular basis to let us know exactly what was happening and what the process dictated would happen next.  We don't imagine this was as straight forward as some, but Nancy kept a grip on the situation as it unfolded and closed it out for us.

records.title: Great
records.text: Rebecca Rees was a great support to help progress our sale. Near completion, Rebecca was on the ball following up with the buyers solicitor and keeping us posted as there were some delays from the buyers side. She was very efficient in supporting us. DCLaw use the eWay system and this process was seemless.

records.title: A great experience with DC Law
records.text: A great experience with DC Law, very quick turnaround!

records.title: Just want to say a massive thank you to…
records.text: Just want to say a massive thank you to Jen for all her hard work during our move. Whilst working with incompetence either side of our chain, Jen persisted through some tricky situations. Communication was always good via email and regular catchups on the phone. Thank you once again Jen and we  will definitely be in touch if we are ever mad enough to move again! Mark and Kylie

records.title: Thank goodness for Rachel Samosa who…
records.text: Thank goodness for Rachel Samosa who got the sale over the line after many months & many other names (who appeared to do nothing at all unless chased)The lack of communication between the solicitors, not to mention the client was really bad. The original estimate given for completion was 25 May & here we are 4 months later. Identification which should have been completed at the outset was left hanging. Your procedures seem to be disorganised & the staff deal with issues on a reactive basis instead of being given time to be proactive.I was not impressed with the firm which was recommended by the Co-op, until Rachel took the reins & actually got things done. She was also the only person out of about 5, who answered her phone & answered emails. Before she took over I had left countless messages & sent lots of emails which were never replied to. Thank you Rachel Samosa.

records.title: Myself and my husband were really…
records.text: Myself and my husband were really pleased with the great service we received. The online service seemed to work well and keep us on track with monitoring and completing tasks. Our contact was Kayleigh and although I had very little contact with her (mostly done by my husband as he works from home and has access to his emails most of the time) he didn't complain which must mean she was doing something right. I know towards the end she was key in getting our sale completed. No complaints from me and would definitely recommend and use them again, although not planning on moving anytime soon.

records.title: My case handler has been exceptional
records.text: My case handler has been exceptional. She has kept me upto date at every step. Lisa Rimmer thank you for helping me through what has been a turbulent time.

records.title: Thank you for providing explanations…
records.text: Thank you for providing explanations throughout the process of buying our house - despite them not being what we wanted to hear at times - we are now at the finish line so thank you for your support

records.title: Esme Hible
records.text: My case was the purchase of a retirement flat and my handler was Esme Hible, and generally I was quite happy with the result as completion was on schedule and I didn't develop too many more grey hairs as a result of the process. I chose DC Law as a 'budget friendlier' option and I was aware that the service might not include the sort of full on attention I might desire. Yes, there were occasions when I wanted to speak to Esme about my case and could not get through. Yes, I did have a feeling that a very large number of plates were being kept spinning. Yes, I would have liked perfection, but I wasn't paying for that, sadly. Overall, Esme was fully engaged with my case whenever I spoke to her and as far as I could tell any delays in the whole thing were caused by the seller's solicitors. Esme was clearly doing her best with a high workload.

records.title: Good overall but need to improve their internal communications.
records.text: We dealt with Thamanna who was helpful at the beginning and end in particular in what was a longer than expected transaction. Only point of criticism we have was the sometimes difficulty in getting a message passed. Often I would leave voicemail and it was as if they were never passed on and this was very frustrating. Thanks.

records.title: Thankful for people who know what they are doing
records.text: We had a very complicated and stressful case due to bereavement and a property in a shared complex. Debbie thankfully took charge and drove everything forward for us, professional and knowledgeable in her field. I felt safe leaving this process in her hands.

records.title: Overall it was fine
records.text: Overall it was fine. My case handler Rebecca was really nice and always responded in good time, etc.The only thing to mention is that they could have been a bit sharper about getting together and requesting information / documents from me. But i think that most people would say the same about their conveyancer.Otherwise it would have been 5 stars.

records.title: Overall
records.text: Overall, we were satisfied with the service, which achieved its aim at a reasonable price. I was pleased that our conveyancer, Judy, made arrangements for me to complete documents before I went abroad for two weeks. This was instrumental in helping us to meet a deadline in selling the property. To improve the service further, I think there should be more frequent updates for the client to keep them informed of what is happening, rather than having to seek it out. This would help to prevent frustration as there can be quite long gaps between each stage of the buying/selling process.

records.title: Completion of Sale by Rachel Samosa
records.text: Rachel Samosa took over from Judy Yung who had gone on annual leave during the conveyancing of my late Mums house sale. we had not been told that she was away and we had no communication from Judy but by extremely good luck Rachel picked up her phone when we called DCLaw after our buyers solicitor had no luck in getting an answer. Thankfully Rachel was professional, quick and efficient and just over a week later our paperwork was done with help from Rachel and the sale completed in time to save it from falling through. I wish Rachel had been our conveyancer from the beginning of the work, which started in February 2024. things would have been much less stressful, thank you Rachel Samosa.

records.title: DCLaw, the good and the bad.
records.text: We were introduced to DC Law by Co op Legal Services, the latter were dealing with our late father's probate, the former to deal with his house sale. You'll have to get used to dealing with an app to see progress and view updates, however you will be appointed a solicitor at the outset. You'll have a direct email and a phone number, but we quickly discovered our representative was not communicative, not replying to calls or emails. This led to a complaint, excuses from the company, then a newly appointed solicitor, Rachel Samosa. What a difference! She was efficient, polite, courteous and totally on top of the task. If we had a question it was quickly answered and pleasingly the sale was completed without too many further complications. It goes to show that a company is only as good as those who work for it. Go with Rachel and you'll be in good hands.

records.title: 5 stars to Daisy!
records.text: Our assigned conveyancer was Emma H. She seemed to be incompetent. She always seemed fed up and had a bad attitude. Conveyancing took 4 months which is far too long for a sale with no chain either side. Emma Hill hung onto buyer enquiries for 2 months. Not responding to emails or phone calls. Our Help to Buy valuation almost expired. Us and our buyers became so anxious. The process was so unnecessarily stressful. I am sure this would have been longer if we hadn’t complained to DC LAW directly. Luckily her supervisor Daisy D took over, tied up loose ends, finished the buyer enquiries and completed in 3 weeks from taking over. We thank Daisy so much for moving our case along, for her attitude, her attentiveness and for keeping us updated. 5 stars for Daisy!! If it wasn’t for Daisy I would have rated DC LAW 1 star.

records.title: The first year was wasted due to buyers…
records.text: The first year was wasted due to buyers pulling out.a bit more diligence might have avoided that.once the sale was agreed Megan did a great job in getting the sale over the line.overall I am very happy with the service I got from megan

records.title: Probate House Sale.
records.text: All the Staff involved from DC Law were really friendly and helpful,Keran Bashir;Natalie Sykes;Rebecca Dean and Abi Spears. Paperwork seems to sometimes take a long time to go backwards and forwards,but all went through in a reasonable time.

records.title: Communication
records.text: Whilst the overall experience was satisfactory, having engaged DC Law along with MoveWithUs through the Co-Op I did rather expect there to be more integrated up communications, primarily between MoveWithUs and DC Law. At times I was supplying the same information to both, rather than one. This may have been due to staff changes or the inexperience of staff.

records.title: This is an interesting one
records.text: This is an interesting one. On one hand, we completed in under three months (which having moved from Australia, I now understand is quite quick for the UK - in Australia, that is going at a snail's pace) so I am happy with that. On the other hand, easily the most frustrating thing of all, was the constant texts saying, "You have * outstanding tasks on your eWay file...", these were infuriating. In my opinion, an outstanding task is something you've left for a while and forgotten about. To DC Law, this is a task that has literally just been loaded onto the system that needs URGENT attention. Then I would find myself rushing to get the information across and then, nothing. No thank you, no communication, nothing, just a tick on the stupid wheel thing with colours showing how far you've got. Can I recommend this, please use the phrase, "Hello! We have just sent you some documents to review and action at your earliest convenience. Thank you." Yes, this is more wordy but takes the stress out of it. Another negative thing was the incredible length of time to carry out "searches" - I still have no idea what they are. Lastly, our assigned solicitor was almost impossible to reach. For the first 8 weeks I thought she was an AI robot. Thankfully she wasn't. Three stars is kind of generous but I think this is, on the fact we completed in good time, fair. However, next time, we will be using a local conveyancer.

records.title: Great Solicitors - Not The Best Firm
records.text: My solicitor Jenny Oakes was amazing. She was very knowledgeable and helpful on the phone. However there were usually delays on my case being moved. This was no fault of Jenny's and a firm wide issue.

records.title: Busy times
records.text: I think Rebecca has been very busy as it was hard to make contact but when Cheryl took over things were moving,well done Cheryl

records.title: Amazing lady Corey who took over our case
records.text: Corey who took over our case has been amazing, very approachable, proactive and keen to get the case closed, a definite asset to this company.Our first conveyancer was Nathan who has let us down considerably and the company, unable to contact him, no communication, did not reply to messages, totally held the whole sale up putting us back several months, meaning the house sale took over five months to get to completion date

records.title: All was satisfactory during the   Early…
records.text: All was satisfactory during the   Early and mid stages of the conveyance process, however I had notification of Completion and no mention of Exchange, on the day before Completion there was a mad dash to get everyone to agree to the Exchange, not everyone was available . So a lot of stress which could have been avoided if the exchange signing was done much earlier in the process.

records.title: Our solicitor Gareth Hart was…
records.text: Our solicitor Gareth Hart was excellent, I could alway's get him on the phone and what proved a difficult sale, it eventually went through.However the initial introduction to the company was very frustrating not even being put through by the receptionist, and within a month Gareth was our third point of contact, the  web portal proved very complicated and stressful for someone using it cold.As we where selling my deceased Father-in-Laws property the questions and answers for the info, just were not known or available to me, and as the housing association which part owed the property didn't even have a main phone number the whole process wasn't easy.

records.title: Updated review following contact from DC Law
records.text: Following a poor review I have been contacted by DC Law who have advised me that part of a problem I had was caused by Coop Legal Services, who use this company for property conveyancing. I accept that poor communication between these companies contributed to my experience, however I would advise DC Law to ensure return emails, giving clear instructions, are read and actioned in future.

records.title: In the beginning the communication was…
records.text: In the beginning the communication was lacking but as the time went on we have developed a good communication. Earnest Francis is great, he listens and does  his work properly. However, I found it hard to reach them over the phones as it always put you through the voicemail. Thank you for working on my behalf.

records.title: Communication
records.text: A long drawn out house sale and whilst  Lisa was always polite informative and courteous the one downside is the communication could of been better as sometimes it was weeks before any relevant update or information was passed on

records.title: We got off to a difficult start….
records.text: We got off to a difficult start as we had 4 different solicitors taking over the case. Either being promoted or leaving and it was frustrating not to have someone the whole way through who knew everything that was needed to know. It was difficult to get to speak to anyone at times. Ernest Francis took the case over (the 4th) and although it was hard to reach him at times, he was thorough and worked well with us and the agents in the end to reach the completion date that we needed. Thank you Ernest

records.title: Rebecca Rees was polite and patient…
records.text: Rebecca Rees was polite and patient considering this was my first experience of selling a property.  The sale was due to my mother passing away and was very emotive.  Because of my inexperience of conveyancing,  more direct communication of the processes would have made the experience less stressful. I was being informed of dates by my agent but could not get through to DCLaw for confirmation. Dates came and went without explanation. On completion,  Rebecca was quick and informative.  I explained then about  how being a novice in sales and working full time in social care communication could be better. All said and done the transaction is complete and, in hindsight, my expectation about communication may have been to high.

records.title: Not happy.
records.text: After trying to contact dc law several times in the last 24hours I have resorted to leaving feedback here as it is the only place I can see that they communicate with people.  My completion date is set for this Friday 2nd September, however since this date was agreed on 11th August I have received no contact from dc law and am left wondering if completion will actually go ahead this week. I am desperate to speak to someone but my case handler is out of the office until next Monday and nobody else is answering my phone messages or my emails. DC LAW PLEASE CONTACT ME.

records.title: My house selling journey started well…
records.text: My house selling journey started well (begging of May 2022), Sam Brooks was very efficient in coming back to me and it seemed the process was going well. However, we have hit a road block with our Ground Rent company and it seems that DC Law have lost interest in getting this sorted. I understand they are very busy but after reading reviews we are panicking that this road block won't get sorted and we will lose the sale of our home. Every time we chase we feel like a burden and it seems that they want to help less and less. We really want the sorted asap and an update would go a long way.

records.title: Expected a higher standard
records.text: Although some of the issues were quite minor (however some were not) we felt that the sheer number of issues just kept mounting up.  Consequently we felt that overall customer service was poor, attention to detail was poor, communication was poor and ultimately we were not filled with confidence by the entire process.  Finally a distinct lack of apology when it was quite obvious there were failings, was very irritating.  It's a shame, because some aspects were quite good.

records.title: Frustrated and Worried
records.text: I’ve been quite frustrated with how DCLaw has been handling the sale of my husband’s house, as I’ve been handed from a conveyancer who immediately went on leave, came back and went on leave again. I did receive some help from Lisa Rimmer when I rang up, but she was only covering briefly for my original conveyancer. I was subsequently handed off to a new conveyancer who actually got the contracts exchanged, shortly before my buyer was about to pull out, but now, with a new issue that threatens the deal, I am not getting any response from my numerous emails.

records.title: Better communication is needed
records.text: Better communication is needed. An automatic out of office reply to emails would be helpful if away from the office. At least you would know the email had been received and someone might get back to you at some point.Requesting the Management Pack earlier. It was first requested by our buyers solicitor at the end of May but not ordered until mid July. I believe this held up the completion of sale by over a month. We were fortunate not to have a chain and that our buyer was willing to  wait because they wanted the property.

records.title: Too many cases equals very, very average service?
records.text: The set-up I had using DCLaw and MoveWithUs seems to be dis-functional and, sadly, I would find it hard to recommend either of them. The efficiencies (to them) of having a chain of people involved, and, I assume, too many cases leads to a lack of personal service, lower quality of that service and poor chains of communication - with delays and miscommunications to the various other agencies involved eg probate solicitor and estate agents - to the detriment of the customer. Not totally terrible service but very frustrating.The set-up also seems to be reflected in MWU's high staff turn-over, so not only do the people I deal with struggle to remember me and my case (as executor of my brother's will), but new faces regularly take over exacerbating the problems. In the 18 months or so it's taken to deal with my brother's 2 properties, I have dealt with at least 13 people at MoveWithUs. That said, I must commend Lisa S who has been probably the best I have dealt with. There has been better continuity with persons at DCLaw, so there should be less reason for the level of service received, but sadly not, with continual struggles to recall who I am and what you are selling for me and often days waiting for information. That said, I am grateful or just relieved that we got there in the end....

records.title: Very very slow on answering phones
records.text: Very very slow on answering phones.  Even slower dealing with conveyancing.

records.title: A frustrating experience
records.text: DCLaw were very meticulous in looking after my interests during a long and sometimes complicated conveyancing process. However, the process was longer than it should have been because they were often very slow in responding to messages from the seller's solicitor as well as to email enquiries from me. Also, on several occasions the process was further delayed when DCLaw suddenly raised issues that should have been, and I thought had been, resolved much earlier. I eventually realised that much of the problem was that the conveyancer assigned to me was not qualified or permitted to make decisions or sign off on documents herself. Anything not completely routine had be "escalated" to a "team", which meant that documents could sit in a queue until someone else had time to review them. In addition, it was clear on more than one occasion that whoever on the "team" had raised an enquiry was not aware of what had previously been done or discussed with the conveyancer. I was never permitted to have direct contact with this mysterious "team", which was very frustrating.

records.title: Can someone from dc law please help
records.text: Can someone from dc law please help. This seems to be the only way of getting your attention. You are solicitors for someone in my chain. We are waiting for a final thing to complete which we are getting on for 6 months now. Can you please please help!

records.title: Very disappointing
records.text: First conveyancer was so slow to do any work or communicate with us so requested someone else. She was better initially, 'taking over' our case overnight and catching up with what needed to be done, however, again there was little communication. Received more useful and timely information from our Estate Agent.Admittedly it was a difficult transaction due to problems with an old lease and the Freehold having been bought several years ago, but, at times it appeared they didn't really know what documents were required, or how to respond the buyers solicitors questions. We nearly lost the sale as the buyers mortgage offer was due to expire and it eventually took 6 months to complete the sale, during which time I made numerous journeys of over 50 miles (each way) to obtain signatures on  documents rather than wait for the post.24/8/23 - Despite the sale completing on 4th August (as advised by the Estate Agent) I still have not received any confirmation of this from DC Law !

records.title: Avoid!
records.text: We instructed DCLaw back at the end of September to do the conyencing for a home we had inherited. Throughout most of that time, communication has been poor, and progress extremely slow. Our conveyancer has claimed to communicated with other involved parties, but they have said this has not happened. When I asked to speak to manager and was provided with an email address, I was provided with a list of actions that had taken place, which included several inaccuracies. Last week, I was told that the I'd department had failed to request ID. This was reworded in a written document to stated that my ID was re-requested - it had not been requested in the first place. Four months into this process, we are now being asked for a further document, which is appears most other legal companies do not require. Given this is a probate sale, it is very difficult, if not impossible for me to provide a letter sent to one of the executors at the dress of the property. Had this been requested at the beginning of the process, we would have had time to work this out, but four months in, we don't have time. Understandably, our buyers are starting to looking at other properties, and it looks increasingly likely that our sale will fall through - primarily because DCLaw have failed to request documents in a timely manner, and progress our case efficiently. I would strongly advise against using DCLaw.

records.title: far too slow with very high additional fees
records.text: I sold many property in the UK already, but never took 5 months to completion. And this was a vacant, freehold property. Agreed with buyers in mid- June, completed 17th November! Their prices seems reasonable, but if you add in the extra 4 months mortgage payment due to lack of urgency on DCLAW side, you will be significantly out of pocket. Some example of their less obvious charges: Arrangement fee for indemnity insurance is £70 + insurance cost, electronic transfer fee £105 (1 transfer for mortgage completion and 1 for us). While DC Law seems to have a good online platform, you will only deal with their case worker and not with an actual solicitor. I could give many examples where we submitted documents, and 2-3 weeks later we were asked for these particular paperwork.   Additionally, I had to repeatedly ask my case worker to remove indemnity insurance, what we already bought at the time of purchase and is valid for all subsequent owners of the property. This appears to be mis-selling, specifically as I uploaded these documents and emailed them over as well. It seems the case worker does not have the legal background to understand these. Overall I would not recommend this company to anyone. We had difficulties with a vacant freehold property, where both seller and buyer were keen to move quickly, can't imagine the headache for those selling a leasehold or in a chain.

records.title: It’s a good service but watch out for the price
records.text: The instructions are clear and the service to produce the documents very good.  But the pricing is confusing unless you have an understanding of what is involved.  Their website states ‘ It’s easy to get a power of attorney document from the comfort of your own home.  Affordable prices for everyone at only £99 per document’.  In my ignorance I thought that would be the price of the power of attorney for my wife and I.  NO - if you want both financial and health power of attorney for you and partner then it’s 4 x £99.  In addition in order for the power of attorney to come into force it must be registered with the Public Guardian at a further £82 (subject to reductions for those on low income/benefits) for each power of attorney.  So having originally thought the cost would be £99 I’ve ended up at 4 x £99 + 4 x £82 = £724.  Zenco Legal should make these costs clearer on their website.
