They also helped navigate a somewhat fraught process with the top of the chain threatening to pull out due to delays (not due to Claire or Yana, I might add). When it came to crunch time where we had to rapidly exchange they clearly worked hard to expediate the process (with one email coming from Claire at 11pm!), but not at the expense of thoroughness. My only criticism was that they were at times a little hard to get hold of, either being busy when I rang or taking a while to respond to emails. This is likely unavoidable when juggling many concurrent cases though, and didn't impact the sale, as we have successfully completed. Thank you Claire and Yana!

records.title: Would Recommend
records.text: Would RecommendMy experience was positive with Marianne & Moti.  I received swift responses to emails requesting status updates/queries on the purchase of my property.  Also, Marianne was happy to jump on a call to discuss any questions when requested.  I noticed an error with billing where I was overcharged, however this was resolved and refunded to me promptly.

records.title: Great service
records.text: I've recently used Bishopsgate after reading positive reviews on local FB page. Jayden and Chandini was our solicitors with Jayden being our primary point of contact. He was very prompt and professional in dealing with both ours and buyer's queries and explained the process clearly. Would definitely recommend for a smooth service.

records.title: Generally a good experience
records.text: Generally a good experience, used the firm to do the conveyancing on my father in law's house. The buyers solicitor was very slow to act throughout and my only criticism would be that I needed to push Bishopsgate to be proactive in chivvying them rather than just waiting for something to happen eventually! That said, they were far better than the buyers solicitor throughout the process and didn't spin us a web of lies like they did to their client!

records.title: Thank you Marianna and Zaynab
records.text: Thank you Marianna and Zaynab for your excellent work in conveyancing. As a first time buyer you made the experience much easier than expected. Email replies were quick. Both very Professional and efficient. Thanks again Andrew.

records.title: Great improvement after some unhappy experience
records.text: Further to my review about my unhappy experience written on 22/11/2022, I received phone calls and follow-up emails from the firm. I can see that they are sincere and are willing to improve their work. We are delighted to have all the works getting back on the right track and really appreciated them in going the extra mile to answer our questions in purchasing our property. We are satisfied with the arrangement of the payment for the completion. Big thanks to our surveyancer Stenson and also to the great effort of Holly - they are the real treasure of the firm.My advice to those who want to buy a property using this firm - if you spot any problem, don't wait until it's too late. Tell them once you note anything. They are willing to investigate, willing to change and you can enjoy their professional services. It's always more useful to reflect your opinion while they can still make a change. Don't sit and wait until it's too late.

records.title: Used 3 times, would come back again, however..
records.text: Pros: Easy to work with, everything is communicated electronically to my preference. No hidden fees and professional service. Used the team for both residential sales and purchases. Cons: The communication was sometimes slow and some things seemed to be missed out that caused problems towards the end of the process. Don't support auction purchases. The turnaround time is quite long, although that depends on both seller/buyer parties.

records.title: Could be better
records.text: I'm currently in the process of using Bishopsgate Law for the sale and purchase of residential property. The service has been poor. Lack of updates unless chased and a general lack of transparency on the status of the transaction.

records.title: Negative conveyancing experience
records.text: We have been prompted to leave a review by the firm. Our solicitors were Svetlana and Jyeshtha. Overall we had a negative experience, taking 5.5 months for completion on a 3 property chain.Communication throughout this time was poor, with frequent delays in response. Updates were not provided without frequent prompting. Communication when it did occur was often terse, bordering on rude, particularly communication directed towards my girlfriend, who was left in tears on multiple occasions. Letters and emails to the firm were 'lost'.The day before completion we were informed that our funds would not be released by the mortgage provider. This was again due to poor communication from the solicitors, who failed to respond to queries from the mortgage provider in a timely fashion. This led to a late completion, and a charge of £2000 being relayed to us. Despite this charge being completely the fault of the solicitor, when she informed us of this charge, there was no apology offered, and she advised that WE pay it. We pursued this charge with the complaints team at Bishopsgate, who were lovely, and quickly resolved this issue for us.The receptionists and staff other than our solicitors were very professional and polite (in particular, Holly, the operations manager, was extremely empathetic, polite and helpful). Given this, our experience MAY have been lower than Bishopsgate's usual standard. However, I would not risk dealing with this firm again.Update:Following this review I was contacted by the firm. They provided an apology for the experiences listed above. They provided some background on how the issues were allowed to occur, accepted fault, and assured that their process has been updated to ensure that similar issues do not reoccur. They also offered a goodwill gesture.Their response to the original review was positive, and pushes me towards the opinion that our experience was an exception to the firms usual standard.I've updated my review from two stars, as it originally stood, to three stars following this response.

records.title: Leasehold transaction
records.text: We instructed Bisphopsgate Law to act on a residential property transaction (buying) on a no-chain leasehold flat purchase in a development. We were first-time buyers. We did complete on time but there were errors made and some serious bumps in the road. We lodged a formal complaint when we discovered the errors and were immediately put in touch with their operations team and ops manager.I am grateful to Holly and Ryan who have dealt with us since we reached out. They have gone out their way to work with us to redress the errors, resolve the complaint and have treated us with outstanding customer service. Disclosure: this review has been amended 18 months post-completion

records.title: There was a lack of clear communication…
records.text: There was a lack of clear communication and proactivity for much of the time on our purchase transaction. This meant it felt like we were having to manage our own solicitor as well as the seller's. I also didn't feel that there was much value-add advice, it all felt very procedural.

records.title: Disappointing and Slow
records.text: Myself and my girlfriend are first time buyers still in the process of using Bishopsgate Law for our purchase. So far we have been disappointed with the service provided. We initially chose Bishopsgate Law as the pricing was competitive and good reviews highlighting the speed which they achieved completion. However we have already had our process drag on for nearly 5 months which feels ridiculous given there is no chains involved. There was no communication where someone in the team left and how this could impact timelines, the response and update from the solicitors are slow and only respond after being chased, there were mistakes in requesting data from the wrong company which has added unnecessary time to the process.As it currently stands I would not recommend using Bishopsgate Law to any of my friends of family.

records.title: Formal complaint dealt with well after poor service
records.text: I will start this by saying I have already made a formal complaint, which was swiftly, thoroughly and satisfactorily resolved. However, I feel it’s important for potential customers to have information on the not-so-good experiences to inform their decision about whether or not to instruct this firm. I’m afraid I had quite a difficult and stressful experience with Bishopsgate Law, with poor communication and several errors being made throughout my transaction that caused additional stress. There was also a mishandling of funds on completion day itself, which in my view is wholly unacceptable. It seems like there are some very competent team members in the firm, but unfortunately this was not my experience. I have rated 3 stars because my complaint was dealt with very well. However, overall I could not truly recommend using this firm based on my experience.

records.title: My experience with Bishopsgate Law forSlow Communication Marred Otherwise Competent Service…
records.text: My experience with Bishopsgate Law for a straightforward cash property purchase with no chain was mixed overall. My assigned solicitors Jodie Prospere and Vanisha Solanki were very efficient and communicative during the first couple months of the process. However, after that initial period, their responsiveness slowed dramatically.Emails I sent would often go unanswered for several days, pushing things into the following week unnecessarily. On at least four occasions when I tried calling to speak with Jodie or Vanisha directly, I was informed they were unavailable and that one of them would call me back - but no return call ever came.While there were some complexities that arose from the seller's side as well, I felt my solicitor team was content to let my purchase proceed at a glacial pace without pushing things along. It took over 6.5 months total for the sale to complete on what should have been a relatively simple transaction.Around 5 months in, I emailed Jodie and Vanisha citing the companies complaints policy about the lack of communication. Only after this did their email responsiveness improve to an acceptable level, though there were still delays right at the end of the process due to previous questions/enquiries of mine going unaddressed for months.There were also instances where my solicitors seemed to have already received particular information, yet they re-requested it again later. To avoid any further delays, I simply re-provided that data without questioning it further.Ultimately, Jodie and Vanisha did get the purchase completed, albeit after excessive delays that felt preventable with more proactive communication and follow-up on their part. While their legal work seemed competent, the lack of client-focused service for long stretches was frustrating. I cannot wholeheartedly recommend them unless you have flexible timing for your property transaction.

records.title: they take far to long to reply to…
records.text: they take far to long to reply to documents supplied - then they procrastinate and make mistakes - I have found them entirely unhelpful and incompetent

records.title: Communication Lacking
records.text: Nigh impossible to get a response or update on an open file (through multiple phone calls and emails). A quick 'we're working on this' would suffice.  Communication is severely lacking.**Updated: The team have reached out and corrected the situation. Credit where it is due, they have been good in remedying the situation. In future a call/email should be sufficient in place of having to write a Trustpilot review for a response on an open file.

records.title: Good service but expensive
records.text: Rectified a bad experience and was very good RE customer service related to that. Price was extremely high though in comparison to others and the process made quite complicated.

records.title: Good value for money service
records.text: Good value for money. The lead contact was relatively quick to reply to any questions. Providing a detailed summary of all documents sent would have a been a useful addition rather than just  attaching them to an email which seemed more of an afterthought.

records.title: Essentially overpriced for what you get
records.text: Initially, I was very impressed by the speed at which someone gets back to you. But then I realised this is because they're over staffed, i.e they make up extra roles so that there's someone who liases with you in the beginning then it's passed on to a solicitor who is basically an assistant to the higher solicitor so that you don't have to bother them until crucial points in the dealings. This is great, but obviously comes at a cost! I feel they are very overpriced now when comparing them to others and considering what you get. I especially think all the charges they slap on if you're purchasing a new build are deplorable and outrageous, even quite laughable! I have failed to see what extra work they have had to do that equates to an extra almost £1000 on top.

records.title: Difficulties and challenges overcome by a thoughtful and hardworking team
records.text: The approachability and thoughtfulness of Bishopsgate Law’s employees greatly complimented my first time property purchase. A special mention to Ash and Hass handling my case who were extremely supportive and understanding, especially with my myriad questions. They are both so hardworking and were committed in their service to arrange a satisfactory transaction for me – thank you so much!On this occasion, unprecedented busyness within the property market did mean expected standards were not always met, which is reflected in my rating. However, the firm was very responsive to feedback and proactive in resolving difficulties. This along with the care and value they place on their clients does, therefore, give me confidence to recommend Bishopsgate Law.

records.title: Be prepared to pay your legal fees upfront
records.text: Unfortunately my sale/purchase didn't go through so can't comment on that part but this is the only conveyancers who want their payments up front that I've ever used. Think they should prewarn of this when they send the quote.Its a shame they don't automatically refund when you are due money back as I had to ring them 5 times before I got a call back to refund my payments of £650.10. The accounts dept are available when you are making the payments but you can never get through when you want the money back! I found at the beginning the paralegal rarely replied to emails so had to contact the conveyancer herself to complain about this. They have no online tracking so the only way of knowing what's happening is to call or email. In todays market it seems madness to not be using technology to keep customers in the loopI've since had a very apologetic call from the CEO himself so will be giving them another chance once we resell hoping they improve

records.title: Unexpectedly disappointing but a commendable effort to rectify matters
records.text: As a solicitor (albeit in a different field), I have a lot of empathy for the amount of work that goes into a solicitor's job, with that said, my personal experience with this firm was very disappointing. I chose this firm expecting a good standard and even a high level of service, as one would expect from a city firm and for the rates paid - and, as indicated by the other reviews on Trustpilot.The first time I was able to speak to the solicitor on my matter, despite calling and requesting call backs several times, was 6 weeks after instruction and that was when I was trying to get through to the new solicitor allocated to me. She was not aware a new solicitor had been allocated to my file and questioned me about it. I found the general approach of the solicitors lacking an understanding of client service and quite junior in nature. My impression was they did not like to be asked questions and, at times, responded with undue defensiveness and were borderline rude. As a result, I had to take certain decisions to achieve completion by the stamp duty deadline that otherwise I could have done differently (including but not limited to extending the term of the lease) if BL had performed their role in the ample time we had to take care of matters properly.The firm made some effort to put things right by offering a small discount, although only after asking me to provide further detailed explanation of the issues, and allocating a new solicitor who I was told was senior but really was not. Whilst the small effort is recognised, it did not, does not, quite sufficiently compensate for the stress involved and unpleasant experience.Updated following BL's reply below:BL's reply has been posted after I had already responded to Trustpilot's request for information so that BL can identify which matter this review is regarding.Further update:BL has reached out to me, acknowledged the challenges and offered to do the lease extension (that should have been done as part of the original transaction) at no cost. I think this is a commendable effort to put things right and demonstrates their commitment to delivering a good client experience even when things haven't gone quite right the first time - I appreciate this can happen which makes the follow up and how things are managed after the fact really important. Hopefully, the lease extension will be smooth.

records.title: We unfortunately had a frustrating…
records.text: We unfortunately had a frustrating experience with Bishopsgate solicitors during our first home purchase. The solicitors were slow to respond, made multiple errors in documents, and lacked communication throughout the process. Most frustratingly we were not informed about important details like the use of LISAs for exchange deposits until late in the process. Despite being first-time buyers and having a chain-free sale, the process was far from seamless due to the solicitor's negligence.

records.title: Slow, frustrating process.
records.text: Used Bishopsgate for a house purchase after seeing all the good reviews. We had to chase our solicitor multiple times throughout the process which is exactly what we were trying to avoid! Our solicitor was friendly but confusion and lack of communication across their own team was evident which frustrated things.Emails were replied to with a friendly tone hence the two stars. Luckily the solicitor on the other side and our estate agent were quite proactive at chasing Bishopsgate otherwise I feel things would have taken even longer.

records.title: Disappointing experience with conveyancing
records.text: Honestly not the best experience with my conveyancing. For a start, I never had any emails addressed to me by name which I think is quite unprofessional. Along the same lines, I had to reject several documents due to spelling mistakes on their part.I had to chase my solicitor multiple times, it seems like nothing was ever done with any urgency on their side. Multiple times I had to push them to check things because I was being chased by my EA and the Seller's solicitor. To top things off, on the day of exchange they called too late in the day for everything to be done so it was all delayed until the next day.My conveyancing was done by Claire Ryles and Stenson Farrell

records.title: Their incompetence almost caused the purchase to fall through
records.text: Extreme incompetence and poor service almost resulting in the seller pulling out, would not recommend to anyone purchasing a house.I used Bishopsgate Law as my solicitor/conveyancer for my home purchase, their lack of basic organisational skills and professionalism caused extreme delays with the exchange/closing timeline which almost caused the buyer to pull out of the sale.This includes:- on multiple occasions they sent me to documents to sign with references to other documents which they did not share (eg. Title Register, Fixtures & Fittings, Stamp and Land Duty tax forms, etc.) which delayed my ability to sign the documents they needed me to- they forgot to send me documents that I needed to sign and sent "follow-up" emails to ask me the status of signing of documents they never sent me which caused delays throughout the process- did not file documents with my LISA provider on the timeline they said they would which delayed the exchange by over a week and caused us to miss the date that the seller and I both wanted to close- misrepresented the status of exchange/closing timeline agreements they had with the seller's solicitors which caused the seller to almost pull out of the saleI learned the full extent of their unreliability when I received a call from the agent 5 days prior to what I had been told by my solicitor was the agreed closing date that the seller was going to pull out if they did not hear from my solicitor immediately. The seller's solicitor's had not heard from my solicitor in over a week and were entirely unaware of the supposed "agreed" exchange and closing date. My solicitors claimed that this was "normal" and seemed completely unphased by it, however speaking to many other people who have purchased houses this is not behaviour they have ever seen before.When I raised these issues with the solicitor, he was quick to blame the conveyancer and assured me that everything would be smooth from then out as he was personally taking it over, however he seemed equally disorganised and uncommunicative.As a first time home buyer the house purchase process is already extremely stressful and time consuming, having to babysit the solicitors who are supposed to be the experts throughout the process added unnecessary stress and hardship. I wish I had gone with another solicitor and will absolutely be doing that if I buy/sell a property in the future.

records.title: Purchase of Property
records.text: Very poor service, poor communication, lack of updates, very poor web portal for access to documentation and emails, lack of access to up-to-date documentation.  Still waiting for response for my request for missing legal documents.  Felt was always dealing with junior members of staff.

records.title: I feel compelled to write a synopsis detailing our bad experience
records.text: I feel obliged to write a review to express my profound disappointment and frustration with the level of service we received from Bishopsgate Law during our conveyancing process during the period of August 2021 to February 2022 during the purchase of our property in London. Unfortunately, my experience with this firm has been nothing short of dismal, and I feel compelled to share my grievances.  These have been acknowledged by the firm through a formal written complaint, at the point of writing this review the dialogue is still ongoing.Firstly, communication was a significant issue throughout the entire process. We dealt with several members of the team which resulted in a break-down in communication, continuity, and diligence.  I found it incredibly challenging to get in touch with my assigned conveyancer, and when I did manage to make contact, the responses were often vague and lacked the necessary detail; often this took a protracted period. It became evident that there was a severe lack of transparency in the way information was relayed to me, causing unnecessary stress and uncertainty.  It was also apparent that vital documents and queries were never forwarded to us for review and resulted in a very protracted and stressful process. Furthermore, the overall lack of organisation within the firm was painfully evident, and it was very misleading who we were dealing with at variable times during the process; we received correspondence from at least four team members during the process with uncertainty about the qualification or delegated job title during the process.  It was also becoming evident by the 18th January that Important documents were frequently misplaced and had not been reviewed approximately three weeks before out proposed date for exchange of contracts; this meant the estate agent and sellers became frustrated, exasperated and started hounding us about our Conveyancing teams lack of diligence and meant we had to keep chancing up the issues rather than receiving guidance. This ultimately led to delays and an overall sense of frustration. It was disheartening to witness such a lackadaisical approach to handling crucial paperwork, especially in a field where precision and attention to detail are paramount.The standard of professionalism displayed by your team was sorely lacking. I found the general demeanour of the staff to be indifferent, bordering on apathetic. It was disconcerting to feel like a mere number rather than a valued client who had entrusted your firm with a significant and personal transaction.Another glaring issue was the frequent delays in the process. While I understand that unexpected complications can arise, the lack of proactivity and a failure to communicate these issues in a timely manner only exacerbated the situation. Again, this led to unnecessary setbacks and frustrations.We officially submitted a written complaint with the company in March 2022, which was upheld, and a response received from the Customer relation team.  Unfortunately, further issues have arisen which further highlight the lack of diligence shown during the process and another important factor was overlooked, and essential documents relating to communal areas and fire safety were not shared with us; I have now had to approach the team at Bishopsgate Law to discuss this matter further in Oct 2023. This has been met with frustrating results and I am waiting for a follow-up on the matter I have raised.... In conclusion, I felt driven to provide a synopsis outlining our experiences with this conveyancing firm which had/has been thoroughly unsatisfactory. The combination of poor communication, organisational deficiencies, lack of professionalism, and chronic delays has left me with a deeply negative impression. I sincerely hope that this feedback is helpful for any prospective clients while demonstrating the inefficiencies of this firm which allows for feedback utilised for implementing improvements to ensure that future clients do not endure the same disappointing experience.I do have to acknowledge how helpful Ryan and the senior legal team were when we raised the initial complaint, but this does not make up for the tremendously stressful process we experienced; we are now dealing with further consequences of the poorer service, and I hope this may be addressed in our more recent dialogue. I do have to acknowledge how helpful Ryan and the senior legal team were when we raised the initial complaint, but this does not make up for the tremendously stressful process we experienced; we are now dealing with further consequences of the poorer service, and I hope this may be addressed in our more recent dialogue (17th Oct 2023).

records.title: Some positives, some negatives
records.text: I used Bishopsgate in a recent attempt to purchase a flat in London.Starting with the positives, the price I was quoted was good and the initial process of instructing Bishopsgate was more straightforward than that of another conveyancer I tried to use. They have well-designed forms and document checking was all done via an app.For much of the process the team handling my case were very active in pursuing things – in the face of poor engagement from the seller’s conveyancer – and communicated with me in a clear, timely way.But there was a five week period during which there was lots of staff absence – a mix of planned and unplanned – where communication was poor. One of the reasons I chose Bishopsgate is because they allocate two lawyers to each case, meaning someone can cover if one person is off. In practice, during the periods that my conveyancer was not around, communication from the solicitor covering the case was poor.At the end of this period, Bishopsgate seemed to have difficulty pulling together a list of outstanding enquiries, meaning there was a delay in getting this over to the seller’s solicitor, which I feel meant we lost momentum on the case.Ultimately the sale fell through because the seller pulled out, which I think could easily have happened whether or not there were these issues. But I’d find it hard to wholeheartedly recommend Bishopsgate based on my experience.

records.title: Poor communication and unnecessary delays
records.text: Buying a house is stressful, buying a house with Bishopsgate doubles this. Communication was poor throughout, with many of my emails and queries going unanswered and having to be sent multiple times to get any kind of response. Getting the email chains at the end of the process revealed that queries we sent were often not acted on until we had chased up a second time, delaying the whole process.At one point questions we had for Bishopsgate (that they should have had answers to already) were emailed directly by them to the vendors solicitors, who replied along the lines of "it's your job to do this not ours" (fair enough).Delays in Bishopsgate passing on questions from the vendors meant the vendors disposed of a tumble dryer as they thought we didn't want it (costing us a significant sum to replace) - by the time Bishopsgate got around to telling us it was being offered it was long gone.Things that could have been sorted early on in the process (i.e. money laundering checks) were left until the end, causing unnecessary delays.It felt like herding cats the entire process and then at the end we were sent a multitude of documents, of which some would have been nice to see when first  available as these generated even more questions.The only reason I'm giving two stars rather than one is that I at least am living in the house I bought, even if it is tainted by one of the most stressful interactions of my life!

records.title: Use with caution- a little too unreliable
records.text: Their initial process and contact was clear, swift and informative, which gave me confidence for my purchase, though the radio silence on occasion meant I had to escalate matters by copying in a senior colleague of the conveyancer I was assigned.Pros:-The parent firm is reputable-They seemed to be thorough in requesting relevant information from the vendors conveyancer (who behaved appallingly and to whom my conveyancer was very patient)-When they did respond in a timely manner the email information was relevant and helpful.Cons:-The key report from them had incorrect and generic information in it and even when I asked for it to be rectified (by copying in a partner of the firm) it still had unhelpful and incorrect information in it. It appears they hadn't done the work to get the information on planned work, for instance, or to proofread a previous document they'd used for my report before sending to me.-They were sometimes annoyingly delayed with replies.Some months after my purchase I received confidential information, relating to an unknown couple buying a property, from the department checking buyers' information. I flagged this GDPR breach and there was an apology to all parties but it confirmed my opinion of the conveyancing team as being one that doesn't have the best attention to detail or care for overall accuracy.This is a real pity as there were some redeeming features and people in the team and as I had already dealt with them I would have liked to use them for my upcoming sale and purchase. I'll now have to tackle the landscape of ropey conveyancers again.

records.title: Communication issues
records.text: For the conveyancing aspects, I can't say if that was done well or badly.  I've only ever bought one house, so I've nothing to compare it with.  From the acceptance of the offer to completion took 3 days short of 7 months, for a cash sale on a leasehold property.  Maybe that's normal, I don't know. The contract letter stated that the estimate was 12-16 weeks.  Although it was understood that was an estimate, it also stated "...if there are factors preventing us from completing your matter within approximately 16 weeks, we will advise you as soon as they become apparent to us.".  I can't say that was ever made apparent, I didn't feel like I was advised as to what they were.  It felt like every query that I sent was returned with "awaiting replies from seller".  No details as to when or how often the seller was contacted, or what issues were raised.  I was never sure what was outstanding at any given point.  The whole process was opaque.  Sometimes, emails were ignored.  It transpired that when this happened in December, it was because the primary conveyancer (Shanice) had gone on maternity leave, without telling me.  In fact, she hadn't told the seller's conveyancer either, as I discovered when I received an email from them saying "I am struggling to get an update from Bishops Gate Law for the buyer".  When we finally got towards the completion date, some legal documents were sent to me.  I noticed one of my middle names was incorrect. I mentioned this, and got the terse reply "happy for you to amend" from Gurjit.  When the final bill was presented, it didn't take into account the fact that I'd already paid the "retainer fee" for them to commence the work, a sum of £1,240.74.  I had to tell them twice to adjust the bill.  To summarise, I feel like the frequency and style of communication could have been vastly improved.  I just didn't know what was going on, even after I'd emailed and received a reply.  As they weren't the cheapest conveyancer out there, I was expecting better service.[Edit]I've now spoken with Ryan from the management team, who has taken on board the issues above, and made people in the company aware of these comments. He also says they've changed some practices as a result of this feedback.  That makes me feel like they are seeking to improve, which is positive.

What sets Breytenbachs apart is their OISC registration at Level 3, which signifies the highest level of accreditation in the UK immigration sector. This recognition demonstrates their commitment to professionalism, adherence to ethical standards, and up-to-date knowledge of the ever-changing immigration laws and regulations.

By choosing Breytenbachs for your UK immigration matter, you can be assured of receiving expert advice and regulated assistance. The team at Breytenbachs is dedicated to understanding each client’s unique circumstances, tailoring their services to meet individual needs.

With Breytenbachs by your side, you can navigate the often-daunting immigration journey with confidence. Their deep knowledge of UK immigration matters and their commitment to delivering exceptional service will help you achieve your immigration goals. 

For professional, regulated assistance from highly qualified immigration consultants, Breytenbachs Immigration Consultants is the trusted choice for all your UK immigration needs.

records.title: My family situation was very complex…A complex legal matter
records.text: My family situation was very complex and I needed to get approval for my two sons who had become overstayers by no fault of their own to remain in the UK. Without a doubt we had turned to Breytenbachs who has a outstanding reputation for complex cases such as ours and we were assisted professionally and obviously with excellent legal representation on our behalf a application for private and family life in the UK was submitted and with such a short waiting period the boys extension was approved. There is no other immigration law firm I will use other than Breytenbach. If they can’t then no one can in my opinion. Thank you for making mine and my children’s dream come true.

records.title: Comprehensive, incredible and professional support - Thank you Shakir, Kris, Victoria and Nadia.
records.text: A heartfelt thank you to Shakir, Kris, Victoria and Nadia for your incredible assistance with my citizenship application and my husband's ILR application. There really is tremendous value in going to the best for support and assistance! A special mention to Kris - your patience and professionalism in addressing my billion emails and questions was really appreciated.

records.title: Excellent service from Seshni and…
records.text: Excellent service from Seshni and Anneshia in the Durban office. Took all the stress out of the experience of applying for a spouse visa.

records.title: Listen well and respond to your needs…
records.text: Listen well and respond to your needs appropriately

records.title: Breytenbachs are great!
records.text: Was refers to Breytenbachs by a friend. Needed to do our Settled status applications for the UK for my family and I. The service I received was fantastic. So friendly, so informative and they took care of everything. It was so easy for me and I would recommend anyone thats wanting or needing such works done, use Breytenbachs. Samantha and Laya are excellent and you wont be sorry.

records.title: Breytenbachs is professional
records.text: Breytenbachs is professional, efficient and a joy to deal with. They gave an honest and open appraisal even before taking me on as a client. Once on board they kept me informed at every step along the way. Louise was a delight to deal with, reassuring me at every turn.

records.title: Excellent experience with Breytenbachs
records.text: I have worked with Breytenbachs on my family's two previous visa applications and therefore it was a no brainer to get assistance from the company with my son's British Citizenship application.I cannot fault the service I received from Samantha Caalsen and Laya Strydom in the London office, who were once again highly professional and efficient in dealing with my application. Samantha answered all my queries promptly and was a pleasure to deal with.I was overjoyed to get the email to say my son's application was a success! I couldn't have done this without them and I would highly recommend them and the company.

records.title: We got skills, and service are our priority

records.title: Lacking attention to detail
records.text: I am British and Breytenbachs were helping me with a spouse visa application for my husband. My husband’s application was successful, and he arrived last week, however, I found that Breytenbachs lacked the attention to detail that I would expect from immigration consultants.During our first call with Shakir, he told us that meeting the financial requirements would be difficult because I had already moved back to the UK. He suggested that I delay the start date of my new job until after we had applied for the visa. I could not afford to do this, and having read all the information on the UK government’s website I suggested a different route that I thought we could use to meet the financial requirements instead. This was the route we ended up using, and we were successful. I don’t know why he didn’t suggest this in the first place and instead wanted me to delay my new employment.After that first call we were sent a summary of our conversation. This letter contained multiple errors including the incorrect nationality of my husband and a price that was higher than the price we had agreed on.While gathering documentation for the application we had the following issues:•	We were asked to provide a copy of my husband’s UK visa, even though he doesn’t have one•	Since we had spent time apart over the past 15 years, I was asked to submit screenshots (from every Mon, Wed & Fri) of our conversations on social media covering a total period of 30 months. Instead, I downloaded the transcript of the conversation directly from the social media website and submitted this in pdf format. I asked Nadia five times over the course of two weeks if this format was acceptable and I also called and spoke to her, but she did not give me an answer, so I had to spend hours taking screen shots instead, only to find out when reading their cover letter that “only a snippet” of these were submitted as evidence.•	Despite knowing from the beginning that my husband would be applying from the Bahamas, we were told one week prior to application that he couldn’t apply from there as his work permit was due to expire in 5 months instead of the required 6 months. This information turned out to be incorrect and caused us a lot of unnecessary stress.

records.title: Received efficient service to a point…

And when I queried it, I was referred to a consultant who suggested I pay another ninety odd pounds for a Skype consultation. I tried contacting the senior director whose email was provided for complaints. It was "down". I contacted their Pretoria office and was contacted by JP Breytenbach junior. records.text: My rating speaks for itself, it would have been a 2 however ONP redeemed themselves on the last couple of days before completion. They also turned out to be nearly £900 more than quoted, so IF you receive regular contact perhaps keep checking with them if you’re on a budget.

records.title: Majority don't go through this process
records.text: Majority don't go through this process of Mortgage or deed transfer on a regular basis it's more like once or twice in a lifetime. There was a lot too taken in . Simple things like will I get the Land registry paperwork on my name sent to me and by when should I expect it. Hopefully if the case works understand this that the people there are dealing with are not from the same industry and break things down into something simple that they customers can understand it will be getting 5 stars.

Additional information was requested at the last moment resulting an additional 3 days of the expensive SVR rate and again, no explanation. I’ve seen a lot of good reviews here, but sadly due to the lottery of case manager allocation, my review is more negative.

records.text: The app was good and comms quite good however there were fees at the end I wasn't expecting so more transparency was required. I went with this company from a panel referral and the original quote was a lot lower than the final cost.

records.title: Communicstion was poor

Nothing about any of the charges were explained at any point in the process. There was only a phone call at the beginning and end of the process.

records.title: Confusing and left us unsure
records.text: The process was very confusing and we weren’t really sure who we were dealing with particularly with an online portal too. The mortgage transferred over and we hadn’t received a statement or any information regarding payments. We have since emailed with queries and no response.

records.title: Constant chasing for updates
records.text: Constant chasing for updates. Was never told it would be an extra fee to use the online app, we were told to download it right at the start of the journey but when we got the end statement, we had been charged for use of app. Still waiting for the proceeds from the sale now. Completed on Friday. Would definitely go down the route of using a local solicitor in future.

records.title: Very poor
records.text: Communication was poor throughout our sale and purchase. We were forever having to chase our Solicitor for the process to move forwards. description:
The One-Stop-Shop for Accident Management
Winn Solicitors are the national specialists in handling non-fault road traffic accidents, accidents at work and accidents in public places. We help thousands of customers who have been injured or inconvenienced to make a non-fault accident claim every year.

records.title: This review was initially 1 Star, Unnecessary Stress
records.text: Issues with my original insurer (Marshmallow) led to the closure of my policy. As WINNS were assisting at that time, I was informed that the claim with them was also closed “there was nothing they could do and to seek help elsewhere”. I was told this in August 2023.As there was no contact for well over 4 months, imagine my surprise when (23/12/23) I received an email attachment telling me to fill in and sign a document with no further explanation as to what it was for or why they needed something from me after all this time. After emailing the sender back with queries. I was told they were attempting to claim money back for themselves from the accident I was T-boned in when I received nothing and if I didn’t fill in this form then I was in breach of contract and liable despite WINNS closing my claim months prior. The last email I sent was on (05/01/24), I have been met with silence yet again.I’m partially writing this review to see if they actually respond upon seeing this.Since this accident and all the issues that followed, I’ve been in therapy and at my limit. I was hopeful that the new year would be better but here we go again.UPDATE 31/01/24 - The very next morning from this review being posted, I received a call from a manager who informed me that she would now be handling this case. This manager (Kirsty D) was understanding of my troubles given the mixed messages and told me she would do her best to conclude this claim and maybe even retrieve some funds for me due to the damages of my vehicle, she was true to her word and along with a colleague (Sean M) they were able to obtain a settlement for the company and for me personally which I did not expect. They were both extremely professional and were able to conclude this saga efficiently within a few weeks. I am extremely grateful to them for that and I have amended this rating due to this. However, a bad rating shouldn’t have been the prompt they needed to get back in touch in the first place.

description:
First4lawyers is a leading legal marketing collective who can help you get the compensation you deserve after an accident that wasn’t your fault. Our whole team is dedicated to providing great customer care and we’ll only ever introduce you to a solicitor who is right for you. We offer a free initial consultation and only work with fully qualified solicitors who have been through a rigorous pre-screening and vetting process. Our No Win No Fee* service is based on injury, accident and medical negligence claims only and we offer a price guarantee on all other legal services.

*Where we offer No Win No Fee* services typically customers pay 25% of the amount recovered to our solicitors, although this will be subject to your individual circumstances and the actual fee may be less than this but it will never be more.
